faqs.q: What is the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose used for?
faqs.a: The Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose is a cable fitted across a universal air coupling joint, hose to hose, so that if the coupling parts the cable stops the hose flailing. It comes in carbon steel or ss304 in six cable sizes: 1/8" * 20.25" Length; 1/8" * 12" Length; 3/16" * 28" Length; 1/4" * 36" Length; 1/4" * 38" Length; 3/8" * 44" Length.

faqs.q: How do I specify the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose when ordering?
faqs.a: Choose the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose by cable diameter and length from the size range (1/8" * 20.25" Length; 1/8" * 12" Length; 3/16" * 28" Length; 1/4" * 36" Length; 1/4" * 38" Length; 3/8" * 44" Length) and by material (Carbon Steel or SS304). Send us the diameter, length and material you need through our contact page and we confirm the exact part with the manufacturer.

faqs.q: What cable sizes and lengths does the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose come in?
faqs.a: The Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose comes in six cable sizes and lengths: 1/8" x 20.25", 1/8" x 12", 3/16" x 28", 1/4" x 36", 1/4" x 38" and 3/8" x 44". Choose the length to span the joint with a little slack, and the diameter to suit the hose and coupling size.

faqs.q: Which material should I pick for the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose, carbon steel or SS304?
faqs.a: The Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose is offered in carbon steel or SS304, and the notes describe it as a for universal/claw/chicago coupling hose to hose type safety cable for universal, claw or Chicago couplings. Pick SS304 where the cable sits in a wet, marine or corrosive environment and carbon steel for general workshop and site air.

faqs.q: When must a whip check cable be fitted to a universal air coupling?
faqs.a: On compressed air above roughly 7 bar a whip-check cable should be fitted across each joint, so if a coupling does part under pressure the cable stops the hose flailing. The Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose is the hose-to-hose version. The manufacturer publishes no pressure rating for the cable itself.

faqs.q: What is the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose made of?
faqs.a: The Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose is made of carbon steel or SS304. Carbon steel suits general air service and SS304 resists corrosion; tell us the environment if you are unsure which to choose.

faqs.q: What does the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose attach to?
faqs.a: The Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose is made for universal, claw or Chicago air couplings. It loops round both hoses at the joint, so it holds hose to hose if the coupling parts. See our [universal air coupling guide](/blog/universal-air-couplings-explained) for the couplings it protects.

faqs.q: How is the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose installed?
faqs.a: Fit the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose across the joint after making up the coupling and its safety pin or clip, and inspect the lugs and gasket seat at every make-up. A worn lug is what lets a coupling release under load, and the cable is the second line of defence.

faqs.q: Where are whip check cables used on compressed-air lines?
faqs.a: Whip check cables are used on universal-coupling air lines in construction, quarrying, shipyards and workshops. They protect lines feeding jackhammers, rock drills, air tools, sandblast pots and compressor manifolds, where a hose that parts under pressure could injure a worker.

faqs.q: How does the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose differ from the Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Tool?
faqs.a: The Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Hose is the hose-to-hose type, while the [Safety Whip Check Cable — Hose to Tool](/p/safety-whip-check-cable-hose-to-tool) is the hose-to-tool type; both come in the same six cable sizes and in carbon steel or SS304.
